title: Visualizing solutions with slope fields
goal: See what solutions to $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = f(y)$ look like without doing algebra by following a grid of tiny slope arrows (a slope field) from any starting value.

beforeThis.skill: Quick check: slope $= 0$ is a flat horizontal dash ($-$), positive slope tilts uphill ($/$), and negative slope tilts downhill ($\backslash$).

links.label: Precalculus: Equations of lines and polynomial roots

seeIt.title: The Geometric Meaning of Differential Equations (Slope Fields)
seeIt.creator: Dr. Trefor Bazett
seeIt.watchFor: Shows how plotting tangent segments across the plane reveals steady states and solution trajectories.

questions.asking: For each differential equation, sketch its slope field, list all steady states where $\mathrm{d}y/\mathrm{d}t = 0$, and describe the long-term behaviour of the solution starting at $y(0) = 1$.
questions.statement:
Slope fields. Consider the differential equations given below. In each case, draw a slope field, determine the values of $y$ for which no change takes place — such values are called steady states — and use your slope field to predict what would happen starting from an initial value $y(0) = 1$.

  1. $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = -0.5y$
  2. $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = 0.5y(2 - y)$
  3. $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = y(2 - y)(3 - y)$

questions.asking: Spot which of the five differential equations (A)–(E) has horizontal segments ($\mathrm{d}y/\mathrm{d}t = 0$) and positive/negative slope signs matching the plotted slope field.
questions.statement:
Slope field. The slope field shown in the figure below corresponds to which differential equation?

  1. $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = ry(y + 1)$
  2. $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = r(y - 1)(y + 1)$
  3. $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = -r(y - 1)(y + 1)$
  4. $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = ry(y - 1)$
  5. $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = -ry(y + 1)$

figures.alt: Slope field for t from 0 to 10 and y from -2 to 2. The segments are horizontal along y = 1 and y = -1; they have positive slope above y = 1 and below y = -1, and negative slope between y = -1 and y = 1.

questions.asking: Trace the solution curve $y(t)$ through the marked dot in each of the six panels (a)–(f) by following the local slope segments.
questions.statement:
Shown below is the slope field for the differential equation $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = y(1 - y^2)$.

Use the field to sketch solutions to the differential equation passing through the indicated point.

figures.alt: Master slope field for dy/dt = y(1 - y^2) showing horizontal equilibrium lines at y = 1, y = 0 (the t-axis), and y = -1. Slopes are negative above y = 1 and between y = 0 and y = -1, and positive between y = 0 and y = 1 and below y = -1.
Six copies of the slope field labeled (a) through (f), each with a single black initial-point dot placed in a different region of the (t, y)-plane.
